title: There is no single agreed scientific method
summary: The Stanford Encyclopedia says practices vary and that some philosophers reject one canonical toolkit.
body: Brian Hepburn and Hanne Andersen's Stanford Encyclopedia entry on scientific method says observation, experiment, induction, deduction, models, and hypothesis testing are characteristic, that the details vary greatly, and that some philosophers reject the idea of one fixed toolkit shared by all science and only science. The v1 article's seven steps (observe, question, hypothesize, experiment, analyze, conclude, communicate) are a teaching outline. They are not a procedure Galileo or a field ecologist followed as a checklist. Falsifiability, associated with Karl Popper, is one proposed demarcation, discussed in that literature, and it is not the whole of the entry. Peer review is a social check. It does not make a claim true.
